quote: The SPA provides for New York governing law (§ 11.8) and exclusive jurisdiction in New York County state or federal courts (§ 11.9). The Side Letter provides for Delaware governing law (§ 6.1) and exclusive jurisdiction in the Delaware Court of Chancery (§ 6.2)... Because the Side Letter has priority under SPA § 11.11, indemnification disputes are governed by Delaware law and must be brought in Delaware courts... Non-indemnification disputes ... would remain in New York under the SPA, while indemnification disputes go to Delaware. This split could produce inconsistent interpretations of the same agreement.
reason: The memo names Side Letter Section 6 and its Delaware law and Court of Chancery provisions, and contrasts them with SPA §11.8 (New York law) and §11.9 (New York County forum). It says the §11.11 precedence clause makes the Side Letter control, which splits the forum and governing law for indemnity claims and risks inconsistent rulings. It also recommends conforming Section 6 to New York law and forum. This matches the ledger entry in substance.
